name: Hierarchical 3D Gaussian Splatting (H-3DGS)
definition: A method for large-scale reconstruction that trains chunks independently and merges them into a global Level-of-Detail (LoD) hierarchy, addressing memory bottlenecks of standard 3DGS.
summary: Hierarchical 3D Gaussian Splatting is a Level-of-Detail method that organizes 3D Gaussian primitives into a cluster-based octree-like tree structure to efficiently render large-scale scenes by dynamically selecting detail levels based on viewing distance.
